findings.title: A lens selects relations only, so `map --lens flags` has no rule that makes it show the flag with no edges
findings.claim: `LensDecl` has no node-kind scope. A lens is only relation kinds, flow and a level. `map` in its default `summary` detail returns 'counts, top nodes and lifted edges' under a 1,500-token budget. So a Code-level lens over the fixture is the whole workspace's Code level, and the docs give no rule that puts a flag with no edges into the result. That flag is `gift_wrap`, the very entity the toy domain cares about. S10 assertion 2 therefore depends on an unspecified ranking. The same gap affects any new domain whose interesting nodes have no edges.
findings.evidence: contracts.md Pack manifest: `pub struct LensDecl { id, label, relations, flow, level, default, empty_text, empty_action }`, with no kinds. architecture.md 'Lenses and questions': 'A lens is data: a set of relation kinds, a flow direction per kind, a default level and a label.' architecture.md CLI table: `map` summary 'gives counts, top nodes and lifted edges', budget 1,500. architecture.md 'The toy domain pack', assertion 2: '`planroom map --lens flags` shows `gift_wrap` and `new_checkout`'. feature_list.json S10 runs `planroom map --lens flags --json` with the default detail. TRUTH scenarios.S10.flags: gift_wrap has `referenced_from_main: []`, so on main it has zero `reads_flag` edges. `flags.flag` is Code level (architecture.md), and the fixture has about 84 files plus commits, endpoints, sections and states at Code level. The KICKOFF S10 tier is B.
findings.failure_scenario: `planroom map --lens flags --json` on the fixture with both packs added returns the summary page of Code-level nodes, ranked by lifted-edge count. routes.ts and new_checkout carry the only `reads_flag` edge. gift_wrap has degree 0 and is cut by the budget, or is ranked among roughly 200 unrelated Code nodes. The S10 assertion 'shows gift_wrap and new_checkout' fails, or passes only through an ad hoc rule special-cased for the test. A future observability-style lens shows the same blind spot: alerts or dashboards with no edges disappear.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `kinds: Vec<String>` to `LensDecl`: the node kinds the lens is about. Under a lens, `map` at the lens level shows nodes of those kinds plus nodes incident to the lens's relations, each with its parent chain as context. The summary always lists lens-kind nodes before other top nodes, within the budget, with `meta.next` past it. Declare `kinds = ["flags.flag"]` in the toy pack, and add a test that an edge-less `flags.flag` appears in `map --lens flags --json`. Record the change in DR-15 or DR-46.

findings.title: Decision prechecks can't read graph structure, so the S10 toy kind asks a person a fact the graph already knows
findings.claim: The two docs disagree on `when`. Architecture says it has the `filter` shape's form, which includes `with_edge` and `without_edge`. The contract restricts it to field predicates over props that built-in extractors precompute. Under the contract form, an out-of-tree pack cannot write a structural precheck, because it cannot add a built-in extractor. As a result the toy kind `flag_stale` puts a factual question to a person: 'Is this disabled flag referenced by no code on the default branch?' The engine can answer that exactly from `flags.reads_flag` edges. This breaks principle 1, and it makes the S10 example a template for the wrong pattern.
findings.evidence: architecture.md 'The decision loop': 'Predicates are structured TOML (...), the same form as the `filter` shape's parameters' and 'A precheck that needs more than a field reads a prop a built-in extractor precomputes'. The filter shape's parameters are 'node kinds, prop predicates, `with_edge` and `without_edge`'. contracts.md DecisionKind: `pub when: Predicate, // { field = value } or { field = { lt | gt | in = ... } }, over fields and props built-in extractors precompute: placed_by_rule, touched_after_anchor`. DR-63: '`when` reads props that built-in extractors precompute.' architecture.md toy pack: `flag_stale` ('Is this disabled flag referenced by no code on the default branch?', `person` stakes, so it deals a card). KICKOFF principle 1: 'Interrupt a person only for decisions only they can make' and 'Never ask what a good default could answer.' TRUTH scenarios.S10.flags records `referenced_from_main: []`, a deterministic fact.
findings.failure_scenario: After `pack add`, `planroom decide` deals the person a card for `gift_wrap` asking whether it is referenced on main. Jev's pick is pre-selected, so a model is asked for a fact the actual layer already holds. The answer changes nothing the person cares about. A pack author copying the S10 example, say a 'which owner?' or 'is this unmonitored?' kind, has to send every candidate to Jev and then to a card, because they can't express 'has no incoming edge X' as a precheck without a core change.
findings.proposed_fix: Make `when` the `filter` shape's predicate in the contract too: field predicates plus `with_edge` and `without_edge` (relation kind, direction, layer), evaluated by the kernel over the folded model. Keep precomputed props only where the fact really needs extractor-side data, such as `touched_after_anchor`. Recast `flag_stale` as a decision only the person can make: `when = { "props.enabled" = false, without_edge = { relation = "flags.reads_flag", direction = "in" } }`, with the card 'gift_wrap is off and unused on main. Remove it / Keep'. S10's 'a flag_stale card exists for gift_wrap' still holds. Fix the contract comment and DR-63 to match.

findings.title: Editing or moving an out-of-tree pack's files blocks every write in the workspace until a person re-runs `pack add`
findings.claim: The store records each out-of-tree pack's path and content sha256, but the engine loads the pack from its live directory. Any change to that directory changes every process's resolved set: an edit while the author is iterating, a `git pull` of the pack's repo, or the directory being removed (the S10 test itself uses `$TMP`). Every process then refuses every write with `packs_mismatch`, whose retry class is `never`. That covers scans, canvas edits through `serve`, mod tool calls and agents. The only way out is a person-only command, which can't be a one-tap card. One file edit outside the workspace makes the whole workspace read-only.
findings.evidence: architecture.md 'What a pack is': 'The store's `meta` records the resolved pack list (each pack's ID, version, path and content sha256)...' and 'A process whose resolved set differs from the record refuses writes with `packs_mismatch`. A long-lived `watch` or `serve` reloads its packs once and retries... A hand edit of the config counts only after `pack add` or `pack remove`.' contracts.md error registry: `packs_mismatch | unavailable | 7 | never`, with a hint naming `planroom pack add`. `pack add` is person-only by press, typed `/room` or `/dev/tty` (DR-62). KICKOFF principle 1: 'Make those decisions cheap: pre-decided, batched, explained in one line, one tap to confirm.' R10: 'every surface updates live'. Principle 2: Planroom is 'run mostly by agents'.
findings.failure_scenario: A person adds `~/src/acme-packs/flags` and later runs `git pull` there, which changes `pack.toml`. The next commit-triggered rescan fails with `packs_mismatch`. The canvas tab's edits stay pending in localStorage, and the implementer's `handoff report` and the curator's proposals fail with retry `never`. Nothing surfaces as a card, so the workspace stays read-only until the person finds a terminal or types `/room pack add` with the exact path. If the directory was under `/tmp` and has been cleaned, loading fails outright. The S10 evidence run, 'the Write a pack guide followed from a clean directory', hits this on its first edit after adding the pack.
findings.proposed_fix: Have `pack add` copy the validated pack into `DATA_ROOT/packs/<sha256>/`, or into the store, and load only from that copy. The recorded set is then immutable and self-contained, and nothing outside the workspace can change it. A later change at the source path raises one person-only card, 'Pack flags changed on disk (3 files): Update / Keep current', pre-selected to Keep, and writes keep working meanwhile. Keep `packs_mismatch` for real engine or built-in version skew only. Add tests: editing the source dir of an added pack refuses no write and deals one card, and deleting it changes nothing until the person removes the pack.

findings.title: Several listed 'pack questions' are not shape pipelines, so they hide core special cases, and agents can't discover what a pack added
findings.claim: Questions are said to be pack data built from a fixed set of twelve kernel shapes. Yet `kinds` (code), `stage S` and `lint` (plan), `drift` (machines) and `missing` (artifacts) map to no shape. `kinds` returns pack metadata, `stage` returns a method checklist and lint state, and `drift` is a diff. So the engine must special-case these by pack question ID. S10 assertion 1 relies on `ask kinds`, which the docs never define. Nothing lists the loaded lenses and questions with their arguments either. An agent can't learn that an out-of-tree pack added a question or a lens, against principle 2's 'every capability reachable... skills that teach agents when to use each'. The doc's own bar for shapes, 'two packs need it', is also unmet by `machine`, `checks`, `compare`, `order`, `subgraph` and `tree`, each used by one pack.
findings.evidence: architecture.md: 'A question is a named pipeline of one to three kernel query shapes'; 'A new question is pack data. A new shape is a kernel change, so the bar for one is that two packs need it.' contracts.md: `pub enum Shape { Node, Find, Neighbors, Path, Why, Filter, Compare, Order, Subgraph, Tree, Machine, Checks }`. The v0.1 packs table lists questions `kinds`, `stage`, `lint`, `drift` and `missing`, and the CLI `ask` row lists `stage S` and `kinds`. Toy pack assertion 1: '`planroom ask kinds` lists `flags.flag` only when the toy pack is loaded.' `AskReq` is never specified.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer writes `match question { "kinds" => ..., "stage" => ..., "drift" => ... }` in `app`. Core now names pack question IDs. Unloading or replacing those packs leaves dead branches, and a pack author can't write a question of that sort. An agent in a session with the flags pack loaded can't find a `flags` question or lens from the tool descriptions or skills, which are generated at build time. It falls back to reading pack files, spending tokens on what one metadata call should answer.
findings.proposed_fix: Move pack introspection out of the code pack. Make `ask` with no question, a Lenses-idea catalogue behaviour, return the loaded kinds, lenses and questions with their `args`, one-line summaries and owning pack, generated from pack metadata, and have the `room` skill point to it. For `stage`, `lint`, `drift` and `missing`, either add the shapes they use (a `diff` step and a `lint` step) to the `Shape` enum explicitly, or make them catalogue leaves under their idea, not pack questions. Restate the shape bar in DR-15 to match the shapes that actually ship.

findings.title: Hints and linkers are closed to out-of-tree packs, so a new cross-repo relation domain is a core change
findings.claim: Most relations need hints joined across repos, and only built-in Rust linkers join them. An out-of-tree pack may declare `[[hints]]`, but they join nothing: a declared feature with no effect. Domain logic for the v0.1 packs (OTel name mapping, compose host resolution, deploy matching, machine pairing) lives in `planroom-extract`, which S10 defines as core. Aliases and `@ext:` nodes cover simple same-key joins. Any domain whose relation needs a multi-hint join still needs a new built-in, for example a gRPC client whose target comes from compose env, or a Kafka topic with brokers from config. That is the opposite of R11's 'New domains plug in as packs without core changes'.
findings.evidence: architecture.md 'What a pack is': 'An out-of-tree pack emits existing hint kinds... A hint kind it declares itself joins nothing, because only built-in linkers join hints; a new join is a new built-in linker.' 'Hints and linkers': 'Most relations the truth lists need evidence from several places at once... built-in linkers join them'. DR-9 Users: 'a pack can't do what the declarative runner and built-ins can't'. DR-13 or architecture S10 item 5: core includes `extract`. KICKOFF R11 and R1 ('adding a language never touches the core').
findings.failure_scenario: A user writes a `grpc` pack: client stubs emit `grpc.call{service}` hints and servers emit `grpc.serve{service}`, with addresses from compose env. The pack validates, and `doctor --pack` passes because extractors emit hints. But no edge ever appears and nothing warns. The user learns from the docs that they must patch `planroom-extract` and rebuild the engine.
findings.proposed_fix: Pick one of two options and record it in DR-9. (a) A single declarative `join` linker in pack data: `[[linkers]] join = { left = "grpc.call", right = "grpc.serve", on = ["key"], resolve_host = "code.url" (optional, reusing runtime_wiring's container resolution), emit = { edge = "grpc.calls", from = "left.container", to = "right.container" } }`, with evidence the union of the joined hints. (b) Make `[[hints]]` in an out-of-tree pack `pack_invalid` unless a declared linker consumes them, and have the 'Write a pack' guide state the limit, with the alias and `@ext:` pattern for same-key joins. Either way, a declared feature must not silently do nothing.

findings.title: No pack field carries visual encoding, so the TypeScript surfaces must hard-code built-in kind and lens IDs
findings.claim: The design language colors blocks by container kind and yarn by relationship kind. But `KindDecl` has only `icon`, `LensDecl` has no color, and `MapNode` carries `kind` with no role or tone. So `@planroom/ui` can only color blocks and yarn by switching on built-in IDs such as `code.service`, `code.datastore` and `observability.infra`. An out-of-tree pack's Container-level kind or lens, such as the S10 `flags` lens, gets undefined styling. Meanwhile domain names go into TypeScript packages that no domain-free check scans.
findings.evidence: design-language.md tokens: `--block-service`, `--block-library`, `--block-store` ('Datastores and queues'), `--block-infra` ('Tooling and observability'); 'Block colors encode container kind'; the Lenses row: 'Colored yarn strung between pegs, one color per relationship kind.' contracts.md: `KindDecl { ..., icon: Option<String>, ... }`, `LensDecl` with no color field, and `MapView.nodes: Vec<MapNode> // id, kind, name, level, parent, counts, position, ghost, claimed_by`. repo-layout.md: `domain_free` covers only the Rust `kernel` and `contract` crates.
findings.failure_scenario: With the flags pack added, the canvas lens switcher shows `flags` with a fallback or missing yarn color, which may fail `contrast_meets_the_bar` or render invisible on felt. A `kafka.broker` Container kind from a third-party pack draws as an unstyled block. A track that adds `if (kind === 'code.queue')` to `@planroom/ui` passes every boundary check.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `tone` to `KindDecl`, a closed enum mapping to existing tokens (`service | library | store | infra | neutral`, defaulting to the role's or `neutral`), and `yarn` to `LensDecl`, an index into a fixed, contrast-tested palette. Carry both on `MapNode` and `LiftedEdge`, so surfaces style only from the view model. Add a TypeScript literal check that `packages/ui` and `packages/canvas` contain no built-in kind or lens ID.

findings.title: The two literal scans are over-broad and will fail on legitimate code
findings.claim: Two scans are too broad. First, the R16 `domain_free` scan fails on any string literal in `kernel` or `contract` that equals a built-in kind or relation name without its prefix. Those bare names include common kernel vocabulary: `person` (also the Actor prefix the contract must parse), `repo`, `workspace`, `commit`, `file`, `state`, `step`, `machine`, `image` and `tag`. Second, S10's 'no core change' scan matches `\bflags\.[a-z_]` and `\bruby\b` anywhere in the shipped crates and `packs/`. That catches ordinary Rust such as `flags.push("--no-ext-diff")` in the git adapter, or an `en.toml` hint naming the shipped Ruby pack. Both gates will fail spuriously, and the fix then becomes renaming code to satisfy a regex.
findings.evidence: repo-layout.md `boundaries.toml`: `domain_free = ["kernel", "contract"] # no string literal ... equals a built-in pack kind or relation name, with or without "<pack>."`. architecture.md v0.1 packs: code kinds include `workspace`, `repo`, `person`, `commit`, `file`; artifacts include `step`, `section`; machines include `machine`, `state`. Actors are `person:<os-user>` (architecture.md Actors). feature_list.json S10: 'a source scan of core ... for the toy packs' identifiers (\bruby\b, \.rb\b, \bflags\.[a-z_], flag_stale, reads_flag)'. DR-13: 'the release archive ships `examples/packs/ruby`', so help text naming it is likely.
findings.failure_scenario: The contract's `impl FromStr for Actor` matches `"person"`, and `cargo xtask check boundaries` fails CI (S14 'CI is green', S15). Or `extract::git` builds `let mut flags = vec![...]; flags.extend(...)`, and `s10_extensibility.rs::no_engine_source_mentions_the_packs` fails tier B S10 with no real coupling. A track works around it by renaming variables or adding exemptions without a record.
findings.proposed_fix: For `domain_free`, match prefixed names (`code.service`) always, and bare names only from an explicit list in `boundaries.toml` that excludes kernel vocabulary (actor kinds, levels, ID namespaces, shape and parameter names), with a self-test for both. For S10, scan for the toy packs' exact identifiers as quoted literals: `"flags.flag"`, `"flags.reads_flag"`, `"flag_stale"`, `"ruby/ruby-http"`, `"ruby/ruby-script"` and `"rb"` as an extension. Rely on the binary-identity proof for the rest.

findings.title: Kernel roles add a mechanism that buys no extensibility in v0.1
findings.claim: Each of the three roles is bound exactly once by a built-in pack (code or plan), and a second binding is `pack_invalid`. So no pack, built-in or out-of-tree, can ever rebind one. The role machinery exists only so the kernel avoids naming three kinds: the `Role` enum, `Subject::Role { role, key }`, the rule that `retarget` is valid only on a person-stakes role subject, the unbound-role-to-Diffs path, and binding validation. That is the problem DR-45 solved for node kinds by making them kernel vocabulary. Two mechanisms for 'things the kernel needs' are more than R11 or R16 require.
findings.evidence: architecture.md 'A decision kind', the Kernel roles table: `rescan.retarget` bound to `code.override_retarget`, `reconcile.residual` to `code.mismatch_class`, `attach.target` to `plan.attach_target`; 'Two packs binding one role is `pack_invalid`.' DR-45 (kernel kinds as vocabulary; 'a second role mechanism' rejected for kinds). DR-63 (`Subject::Role`, `Effect::Retarget` limited to role subjects). KICKOFF constraint 'Code. Minimal: no speculative abstractions'.
findings.failure_scenario: An out-of-tree pack that wants a better reconcile-residual classifier can't provide one, because binding is `pack_invalid`. Meanwhile every contributor must learn roles, role subjects and the retarget validity rule to change one of three fixed decisions. The indirection is exercised by tests but by no real extension.
findings.proposed_fix: Pick one direction and record it in DR-17. (a) Declare the three as kernel decision kinds (`kernel.override_retarget`, `kernel.mismatch_class`, `kernel.attach_target`) in an embedded kernel data file with their evals, like `kernel.item`. That removes `Role`, `Subject::Role` and the binding rules, and lets the plan pack narrow `attach_target` with a `when`. (b) Keep roles, but let a pack's binding override a built-in's in load order, so the seam earns its cost. Option (a) is simpler.

verdicts.reason: Nothing in the docs covers it. A lens is defined only by relation kinds, flow and level, and `map` summary gives 'counts, top nodes and lifted edges' with no rule for which nodes count as top or which nodes a lens is about. On main, gift_wrap has no `reads_flag` edge. Its only tie to anything is containment under flags.yaml, so a lens built from relations alone has nothing that tells it apart from about 200 other Code-level nodes. The `map` row also doesn't say that `--lens X` without `--level` defaults to the lens's level, so the command could even lift to the top level, where no flag shows at all. S10 is tier B and asserts that gift_wrap is shown, so this is material.
